round1.finding: money ~= consequence in weight; unusual wording counts for little

round2.finding: topic label is NOT the signal — health ranked last here yet 2nd in round 1. Reach is.

reach.conclusion: reach must be read, not pattern-matched; hand-coded figures were partly my own judgement fitted to the answers

round3.era: 2010-2026 only, to remove the recency confound
round3.user_note: felt like it was mostly money sums
round3.sample_fault: 10 of 16 named a sum — a fair criticism of the sample
round3.finding: NOT money-led. $152.6M, $144.8M and $50M all placed in the bottom half; a $0 community garden placed 2nd. $210M for General Hospital ranked 1st while $144.8M for one address ranked 13th — same order of money, opposite ends of the list. Reach again.

conclusion: Three rounds, three angles, one dimension: how much of the city a decision touches. Money and completion matter but are secondary. Reach must be read per record and stored; it cannot be pattern-matched.

round4_edges.confirmed: a public asset GAINED (Mint Plaza, 1st) beats one GIVEN AWAY (Hayward Playground to the 911 centre, 9th)
round4_edges.refuted_scope: citywide crossing signals ranked 8th, BELOW a one-block one-way plan at 4th — scope alone does not lift a street rule
round4_edges.refuted_honour: Avery Street renamed for Reverend Boswell 11th, James Alley to Rose Paks Way 5th — it is whether the city knows the name, not that a person is honoured
round4_edges.refuted_floor: procedure landed mid-list, not at the floor

stated_rules: adopted weighs much more than proposed, but a huge or significant proposal still ranks high
money into daily-life infrastructure (hospital, library) beats a similar or larger sum on a housing bond
housing and shelter are near the top, but housing PEOPLE differs from a housing BOND at an address

keyword_attempt.result: WORSE than the previous score on 2 of 3 testable rounds

outcome: the stated rules become a rubric applied by reading each record (IMPORTANCE.md), not a pattern
